title: Urological Supply Program Self-Pay Purchase and Shipping Terms
content:
A self-pay catheter line in the Urological Supply Program costs the quantity multiplied by the program's self-pay price per catheter. Enrolled self-pay patients receive the program's accessory discount off accessory items, rounded to the cent half up per line. Catheters beyond the monthly limit may be bought self-pay where the program allows it. A hydrophilic catheter is furnished at no extra charge where the program's hydrophilic option is yes and is never billed as an upgrade. Shipping by ground costs the program's ground shipping charge, expedited shipping costs the program's expedited charge paid by the patient, and every package is unmarked where the program ships in unmarked packaging.

## Terms in brief

| Subject | Term |
|---|---|
| catheters on a self-pay line | quantity multiplied by the self-pay price per catheter |
| accessory items (bags, lubricant, trays, remover) for an enrolled self-pay patient | the accessory discount off, rounded to the cent half up per line |
| catheters beyond the monthly limit | may be bought self-pay where allowed |
| hydrophilic catheter | no extra charge where the hydrophilic option is yes; never billed as an upgrade |
| ground shipping | the ground shipping charge |
| expedited shipping | the expedited charge, paid by the patient |
| packaging | unmarked where the program ships in unmarked packaging |

## Hypothetical worked figures

- 60 catheters on a self-pay line of the Straight Intermittent Catheter Program (A4351), at its self-pay price of 1.45 USD: 60 multiplied by 1.45 is 87.00 USD.
- An enrolled self-pay patient's accessory line with a hypothetical undiscounted amount of 23.85 USD and a 10 percent accessory discount: 23.85 less 2.385 is 21.465, which rounds half up to 21.47 USD for the line.
- A hydrophilic-coated catheter furnished on the Coudé Tip Intermittent Catheter Program (A4352), whose hydrophilic option is yes, costs nothing beyond the catheter itself.
